title: Domestic Trap / Familiar Space Tightens

source_refs.author: Domestic horror staging tradition
source_refs.title: The dwelling as a tightening enclosure
source_refs.cultural_context: Horror cinema in which repeated rooms stop protecting the people who live in them

observed_structure: A dwelling is first readable as ordinary shelter.
The same paths, doors, and objects recur, and each pass is slightly more hostile.
Leaving or resting no longer restores safety, so the dwelling behaves as a trap.
dramatic_operations: turn a familiar dwelling into a tightening enclosure
repeat domestic paths until repetition itself feels hostile
contaminate shelter by altering the same rooms under sustained strain
cinematic_affordances: repeated architectural lines that grow less comforting
blocking that circles the same route
a slow move that feels like the space is following
house noise that gains force without a visible body
cultural_scope: general domestic-horror staging; a specific culture's house rules need their own provenance
misuse_risks: a creepy house with no change across repetitions
contamination claimed by set dressing alone
copying a famous corridor, carpet, or hotel plan

variables: who still treats it as shelter

transferable_structure: a familiar dwelling tightens through repetition until the inhabitant can no longer treat it as shelter
non_transferable_surface: a copied haunted-house floor plan, carpet, or hotel corridor from a specific film
